registered_before: any model is fitted on LID-DS and any LID-DS score of Pulse or of a baseline is computed
purpose: G3 (public dataset) and part of G2 (real exploits): Pulse's final system evaluated on LID-DS 2021 with every parameter taken from the live system, nothing tuned on LID-DS

data.dataset: LID-DS 2021 (Grimmer et al. 2022), 15 scenarios, recordings of the public Proton Drive share linked from github.com/LID-DS/LID-DS, downloaded 25/10/2026 (15 archives, 87 GB, every zip passed testzip)
data.conversion: sentinel_pulse/lidds/convert.py: syscall entries replayed into the eBPF loader's cumulative frames (full-ID counts, ID and per-thread transition bins as pulse_counter.bpf.c), 0.5 s windows, Pulse's ExtendedFeatureStream unchanged; seccomp skips not recorded by LID-DS (0)
data.splits: the dataset's own: training (fit), validation (calibration), test/normal and test/normal_and_attack (evaluation only)
data.unit: one scenario = one workload; one recording = one container

ml.model: per scenario, PulseExtendedReferenceTree(history=3, alpha=0.001, random_state=73021) fitted on the training recordings' sequences of eligible windows (decode_vector of the 249 features), calibrated on the validation recordings; PulseSupportEnsemble (interval budget 0.05, horizon 30 windows) fitted on the training current windows, calibrated on the validation current windows. All windows used, no cap
ml.decision: the live rule of policy-k2of2-a5-peer30 without the evidence discount (a recording has no replica): window passes when joint_p <= 5 x 0.05/30; alarm when two consecutive contiguous windows pass
ml.scored_windows: windows with three contiguous eligible windows before them, as the live scorer

tripwire: reference = union of syscall IDs of every window of the scenario's training recordings; exec set E (validation-evidence/results-20261021/pulse-stable-candidate/final/exec-set-E.json); a test window alerts when it carries an ID outside both
system: ML alarm or tripwire alert in a window (the final system, owner 25/10)

metrics.per_recording: an attack recording (test/normal_and_attack) is detected when an alarm window ends after the recording's first exploit time; latency = that window's end - exploit time. A normal test recording (test/normal) is a false-alarm recording when any window alarms; alarm windows of an attack recording ending before the exploit are counted as false alarms too
metrics.reported: per scenario and over all scenarios: detection rate (Wilson 95 % CI), false-alarm recording rate on test/normal (Wilson 95 % CI), alarm episodes (windows less than 15 s apart merged) per hour of test/normal windows, latency p50/p95, for ML, tripwire and system
metrics.no_threshold: LID-DS has no registered pass mark here; results are compared with the published LID-DS 2021 results only where the cited paper states the same metric, and with STIDE below

baseline: STIDE (Forrest et al. 1996) on the same splits: database of syscall-name 7-grams of each thread's entry sequence in the training recordings; a test window alarms when one of its threads completes a 7-gram not in the database (any-mismatch variant, no tuning); same per-recording metrics
statistics: Wilson 95 % CI for recording rates; scenarios as clusters for a bootstrap 95 % CI of the pooled differences system - ML and system - STIDE (10,000 draws)
